title: The Wall of Storms
author: Liu, Ken
review:
For people who struggled with the first book I think this one might be more in the wheelhouse of a traditional fantasy narrative and be more appealing to people who had issues with the Grace of Kings. It's less of a fable and legend like the first book and more of a modern plot structure. Also the female characters are way better in this one and often overshadow the male characters in most ways.

I really loved every moment of this one again, even though it's almost a thousand pages I didn't want it to end. I do think I personally liked the structure and themes of the first book more but this one had a superior plot and really interesting politics.

Excited to continue the series and see how it all ends. Liu is really good at giving a full cohesive narrative per book so it doesn't leave you hanging and a lot of the threads are wrapped up with enough to make you interested in the next books.

The battles in this book are some of the best I've read, I really didn't expect that from the series but it's been a nice surprise. The technology and war dynamics are always getting changed up which keeps things fresh from battle to battle and book to book.

The prose is also gorgeous as in the first book, but it felt like Liu pulled back in a lot of ways from the first book and delves less into descriptions and poetic nature metaphors. Maybe some people thought it was self indulgent, but I never did and I loved it. I really liked those sections in the first book, but they're less present here and the plot takes more of a center stage for better or worse.
